classification.habitat: Scrub, forest margins, hedges and moist open sites
classification.distribution: Tropical and subtropical regions of the Indian subcontinent and elsewhere

identification.description: Perennial dioecious climber with rounded to heart-shaped leaves and small inconspicuous flowers.
identification.whole_plant: Slender twining perennial herb or climber.
identification.root: Tuberous or somewhat thickened roots in mature plants; authenticate before use.
identification.stem: Slender, twining, soft to somewhat woody with age.
identification.leaf: Simple, alternate, broadly ovate to reniform, often heart-shaped at the base, with long petioles.
identification.flower: Small greenish-yellow flowers in axillary or clustered inflorescences; male and female flowers occur on separate plants.
identification.fruit: Small rounded drupe, usually red when mature.
identification.seed: Single seed enclosed by the fleshy drupe.
identification.bark: Not distinct in the herbaceous young stem.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Cissampelos pareira has been investigated experimentally for antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory and other activities. These findings are not presented as established clinical efficacy.
modern_information.safety_notes: Use authenticated material and appropriate professional guidance.

viva_questions: Are male and female flowers on the same plant?
mnemonics: Patha = path of a twiner: heart-shaped leaves on a slender climber.
student.quick_revision: Patha (Cissampelos pareira): perennial dioecious climber of Menispermaceae; root is used; cordate leaves and small drupes aid identification.

teaching_points: Demonstrate twining habit and cordate leaf base.
Discuss dioecy as an important botanical character.
practical_points: Observe male/female flowering material separately when available.

doctor.quick_reference: Patha is traditionally used in digestive and febrile contexts; no dose is supplied without a verified classical/pharmacopoeial reference.
key_precautions: Do not infer dosing from this record
Evaluate persistent fever or urinary symptoms appropriately
